newsitem.title: USA: VIDAMED sees Q1 revs of $3.3 mln.
newsitem.headline: VIDAMED sees Q1 revs of $3.3 mln.

text.p: VIDAMED Inc said Wednesday it expects net revenues of $3.3 milllion for the first quarter, up from $488,000 a year earlier and $2.44 million in the 1996 fourth quarter.

The company attributed the higher revenues to increased marketing and sales efforts in the U.S. since it received marketing clearance from the Food and Drug Administration for its TUNA System last October.
VIDAMED did not give earnings estimates.
Analysts on average expect a first quarter loss of $0.22 a share, according to First Call. The loss in the 1996 fourth quarter was $0.29 a share.

The TransUrethral Needle Ablation (TUNA) System, the company's principal product, is designed to offer a minimally invasive alternative for the treatment of symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia.
